What makes Brachiosaurus so amazing?

Holding its neck up high like a giraffe, the Brachiosaurus was a giant plant-eating dinosaur that picked leaves from tall trees. It was over 20 m long.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Brachiosaurus

Brachiosaurus was a giant about 21–26 m long and weighing 30–56 tons. Its most striking feature was that its front legs were longer than its back legs, so its back rose up high in front like a giraffe's and its neck naturally pointed upward. Its bones were hollow and light with air sacs like a bird's, and each day it stripped and ate about 400 kg of plants with its spoon-shaped teeth.

Points worth exploring together

Point out details like the long neck (high leaves), front legs longer than back legs (giraffe posture), the enormous body, and the spoon-shaped teeth. It's fun to talk about it together: "Why is its neck so long?"

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Compare it with a photo of a giraffe and talk about how "they both eat high leaves." Imagining its size (20 m) next to the height of a building really brings home just how enormous it was.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why was Brachiosaurus's neck so long?
A. To pick leaves from tall trees. Its long front legs made its neck naturally point upward.

Q. How much did it eat?
A. About 400 kg of plants a day. It stripped leaves with its spoon-shaped teeth.

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Compare it with a giraffe, and imagine its size next to the height of a building.
